name: The Bombay Burmah Trading Corporation Limited

facts.business: The Bombay Burmah Trading Corporation Limited operates tea plantations in South India, manufactures auto electric components (Electromags) in Chennai, and produces dental products (Dental Products of India) in Uttarakhand, with a branch in Malaysia.
key_risks: Climate volatility and pest pressure (e.g., Tea Mosquito Bug causing up to 25% crop loss)
Ageing workforce and labour shortages leading to delays in plucking and decline in leaf quality
Rising wage costs (7% wage increase translating to ~9% rise in labour costs)
Withdrawal of subsidies by Tea Board of India reducing financial support and export competitiveness
High dependence on imported semiconductors and electronic sub-assemblies exposing supply-chain disruptions
Pricing pressure from OEMs impacting margins
Accelerated technological change increasing risk of product obsolescence
facts.related_party_note: All transactions entered into with related parties during the year under review were in the ordinary course of business and on an arms' length basis and did not attract the provisions of Section 188 of the Act. The Corporation had not entered into any contract/arrangement/transactions with related parties which could be considered as material in nature. Disclosures pertaining to transactions with related parties are given in Note no. 45 of the Notes forming part of the Standalone Financial Statements for FY 2025-26.
